blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

GEOGRAPHY LOCK — flagged at the top: County Line / Glen Valley is ENTIRELY in the Township of Langley. It is NOT in Abbotsford. The sub-area recorded zero attached listings and zero attached sales in September 2026, its feed is individual rural acreage parcels rather than named projects, and no named strata complex of any kind is verified here.
Streets, schools and getting around County Line Glen Valley

items.t: County Line Glen Valley is one of eleven Langley sub-areas in the September 2026 SnapStats data — Aldergrove, Brookswood, Campbell Valley, County Line Glen Valley, Fort Langley, Langley City, Murrayville, Otter District, Salmon River, Walnut Grove and Willoughby Heights. The board community "Langley" combines the Township of Langley and the City of Langley, and this sub-area sits entirely on the Township side in the feed's evidence. A street-level boundary for the sub-area is not verified — no board street-level boundary is published, and none was substituted.

Municipal geography: the Township of Langley, in the rural northeast/east of the Township toward the Abbotsford border; the feed's postal codes run V4W and V1M, and its listing text places parcels minutes from the 264 Street / Highway 1 interchange and from Fort Langley.

County Line Glen Valley is the only Langley sub-area with zero detached inventory in September 2026, and jointly (with Campbell Valley and Otter District) one of three with zero attached inventory. SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, so there is no sub-area median: Not verified at sub-area level. The eleven sub-area rows sum to the community totals in both splits.
The two figures are different instruments at different dates — a September board snapshot against a live November MLS feed — and neither is corrected from the other here.

What the feed actually shows: rural Township acreage — 5 acres, 20 acres, 66.3 acres, 5.16 acres, 8.3 acres and 4.87 acres in the cards' own listing text — with equestrian estates, hobby farms and multi-dwelling farm parcels; there is no attached product on the first page, which matches the sub-area's zero attached inventory in the September 2026 table.
Schools: Langley is School District 35; catchments are address-based.
The community hospital for Langley is Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway (Fraser Health).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in County Line Glen Valley

items.t: ALR residences cannot be stratified — the rule that leads this section: On land in the Agricultural Land Reserve, a residence cannot be turned into strata lots (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). The ALR frame governs any parcel in the Reserve, which is the first check on this sub-area's acreage stock: land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel; a principal residence may be up to 500 m² total floor area; one additional detached residence may be permitted of up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha; a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence and only where local bylaws allow it.

Township SSMUH — stated so it is not misapplied to this sub-area: the Township of Langley adopted Bylaw No. 6020 on November 18, 2024, allowing 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units on lots between 280 m² and 4,050 m², subject to eligibility (inside the Urban Containment Boundary, connected to municipal water and sewer, no heritage designation, not in a Transit Oriented Area); lots over 4,050 m² are not eligible, and NO 6-plex / 6-unit transit tier exists in Bylaw 6020. Most parcels in this feed exceed the 4,050 m² ceiling by a wide margin, so the SSMUH framing generally does not apply to them.

Township secondary suites: under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102 (as amended July 2025), a secondary suite may not exceed 120 m² maximum gross floor area, each principal dwelling unit may have up to one secondary suite, and on ALR lands a suite must comply with Agricultural Land Commission regulations. LIVE CONFLICT, reported with dates and not resolved: the Township's January 2025 secondary-suites guide states suites are NOT permitted in townhouses/rowhouses and describes suites as within detached single-family dwellings, while the current s.

Township coach houses: in Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102, a "coach house" is an accessory dwelling unit located only within the second storey of a detached garage; no size cap for a coach house appears in s. Township short-term rentals: the Township does not issue business licences for short-term rental accommodations; the permitted-use status of STRs under Zoning Bylaw No.

The strata rules, for contrast — they bite only if the same buyer buys strata elsewhere in Langley: Form B (Strata Property Act s. 59) states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance, and a summary of the strata's insurance, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Depreciation reports: since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must obtain one every five years, no deferral by vote. Minimum CRF contribution: at least 10% of the operating fund since November 1, 2023. Rental-restriction bylaws are void since November 24, 2022. 55+ bylaws: SPA ss. 123.1/123.2 — only 55+ is lawful, with exemptions for younger spouse/partner, live-in caregiver, legacy residents and defined child cases (May 1, 2023 expansion). None of this applies to a Glen Valley acreage purchase, because there is no strata corporation.

GST and taxes on an acreage purchase: 5% GST applies to new construction, not resales — this sub-area's stock is resale acreage product. The First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate (Bill C-4) rebates 100% of GST up to a $1 million price (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5 million, for agreements signed on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031; CRA's Excise and GST/HST News No. 122 states Bill C-4 received Royal Assent on March 13, 2026. The older GST New Housing Rebate (36%, maximum $6,300, $350,000–$450,000 phase-out) still exists.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), if a park home elsewhere is compared instead: pad-rent increases are capped at 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027. No park is verified in this sub-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about County Line Glen Valley

items.t: The address says Langley, the search results say Abbotsford — and both will mislead you if you stop there. This sub-area adjoins Abbotsford, so Abbotsford's condo buildings surface in the same searches, but every Abbotsford complex is in a different municipality, under a different zoning bylaw (Abbotsford No. 2400-2014 versus Township No. 2500) and a different tax notice.

This is the only Langley sub-area with zero detached snapshot inventory in September 2026, and jointly (with Campbell Valley and Otter District) one of three with zero attached inventory — checked against all eleven sub-areas. A parcel-by-parcel market with months like that has no sub-area median or pace figure to anchor on; SnapStats publishes medians at community level only.

The Township's own suite documents disagree with each other. The January 2025 secondary-suites guide and the July 2025 Zoning Bylaw s. 102 definition conflict on suites in townhouses and rowhouses. Anyone quoting the guide on an attached-home suite question in the Township is quoting the older, superseded-on-this-point document — and the same conflict matters if a Glen Valley buyer later buys attached product elsewhere in the Township.

A decommissioned suite is disclosed in this sub-area's own feed. One first-page card states its suite was decommissioned by the Township — a reminder, in the sellers' own listing text, that suite legality here is enforced and document-based, not assumed from a floor plan or a listing photo.

Second dwellings are the recurring pitch, and the ALR is the recurring limit. In-law suites, second homes, a mobile home as a second dwelling, guest suites over barns and large shops appear across the first-page cards — and on ALR parcels every one of them runs into the same frame: a 500 m² principal-residence cap, a suite only inside the principal residence, and a 90 m² / 186 m² cap on an additional residence.
The recorded SD35 locator samples are urban (Willoughby and Fort Langley village).
Glen Valley Regional Park is named as the recreation anchor in the page copy only.

The feed and the snapshot disagree, and neither is wrong. The live feed showed 21 results on Nov 1, 2026 while the September 2026 snapshot records zero detached inventory — different instruments at different dates. A buyer who quotes either figure as "the market" without its date and instrument is quoting half a fact.

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default (and only verified) form: equestrian estates, hobby farms and multi-dwelling farm parcels trade as whole fee-simple parcels — no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees. A multi-dwelling farm parcel is a freehold land purchase with dwellings on it, not attached stock.
Bare-land strata: none verified: Any claim of a bare-land strata lot here is not confirmed.

Lot character, only: rural acreage parcels (sizes above are listing text, not a published lot profile); a Township-wide or sub-area lot-size/age/style profile is not verified — no official source publishes one. Zoning is Township Zoning Bylaw 2500 lot by lot; the parcel's zone for a specific PID is a Township confirmation.

R-CL discipline (standing correction, carried so it is never misapplied): Township Zoning Bylaw 2500 s.403 R-CL = 220 m² minimum lot area / 464.5 m² maximum LOT area. No "355 m²" figure exists in the bylaw and it is never carried.

ALR vs non-ALR split: no split is published and none is stated. Glen Valley is farm ground and the first check on any parcel is its reserve status on the ALC maps by PID or civic address; feed text (a 66.3-acre estate citing Township-approved plans for a new secondary home; a 20-acre parcel with two homes plus a mobile home as a second dwelling; a court-ordered sale disclosing a suite decommissioned by the Township) is listing text only, not verification.

faq.q: Is County Line Glen Valley in Abbotsford or Langley?
faq.a: Langley — the Township of Langley, entirely.

faq.q: Are there any condos or townhomes in County Line Glen Valley?
faq.a: Langley's attached stock is in its urban sub-areas (Willoughby Heights, Langley City, Walnut Grove, Murrayville).

faq.q: What is the median price in County Line Glen Valley?
faq.a: Those are community figures, not this sub-area's figures. Price a Glen Valley parcel parcel-by-parcel, with a longer look-back and wider geography than a community-median shortcut.

faq.q: Can a Glen Valley acreage have a second home or a suite?
faq.a: Parcel by parcel. On ALR land, the ALC frame allows one principal residence up to 500 m² plus at most one additional detached residence of 90 m² (parcels 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), with a suite only inside the principal residence; under Township Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 a secondary suite is capped at 120 m² gross floor area, one per principal unit. Confirm the parcel's ALR status and permits before valuing any second dwelling.

faq.q: A listing mentions approved plans for a second home, and another mentions a mobile home as a second dwelling. Can I rely on that?
faq.a: No — treat both as document claims, not rights. The feed itself contains the cautionary version: a court-ordered sale card disclosing a suite the Township had decommissioned. Verify approved plans, suite legality and any mobile-home-as-dwelling status against Township records and the ALC frame before subjects come off.

faq.q: Is County Line Glen Valley in Abbotsford?
faq.a: No — entirely Township of Langley, in the rural northeast of the Township toward the Abbotsford border.

faq.q: What is actually for sale here, then?
faq.a: Township acreage: equestrian estates, hobby farms and multi-dwelling farm parcels — the five guide cards read ran from a 5-acre family home to an 8.3-acre equestrian property.

faq.q: Why can't an ALR farm just be stratified into townhouses?
faq.a: Because the law bars it: ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)).

faq.q: A listing says the suite was decommissioned — what does that mean for me?
faq.a: Verify every suite on paper (120 m² cap, one per principal unit, ALC compliance on ALR land) before valuing it.

faq.q: A card says the suite was decommissioned by the Township — what does that mean for me?
faq.a: Verify every suite on paper — permits and Township records — before pricing suite income.

faq.q: What is County Line Glen Valley, and what does this guide cover?
faq.a: County Line Glen Valley is a Fraser Valley board sub-area in the Township of Langley. The guide page is written about Glen Valley — farm country on the south shore of the Fraser River in Langley's northeast corner, toward the Abbotsford border — which on MLS® is part of that sub-area, one of eleven Langley sub-areas in the SnapStats data (SnapStats, September 2026)

faq.q: Can a Glen Valley acreage have a second home or a suite?
faq.a: It depends on ALR status and Township zoning, parcel by parcel. On ALR land, the ALC frame allows one principal residence up to 500 m² plus at most one additional detached residence of 90 m² (parcels 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), with a suite only inside the principal residence; under Township Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 a secondary suite is capped at 120 m² gross floor area, one per principal unit (~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/rules-gaps-2026-11-01.md, read 2026-11-01).
